rationale.text: The test has one requirement with two routes: the effect's frequency is below three per second, or the total cumulated area of the effects is at most 21824 pixels. Measuring a frequency and an area is mechanical in principle, but the test applies only to images and multimedia elements that cause an abrupt change of brightness or a flash effect, and the glossary defines that only as an alternation of relative luminance that may cause seizures when large enough and in a specific range of frequencies. It gives no luminance threshold that makes a change abrupt and no frequency range, so code cannot decide from the official text which alternations are in scope. A check that faulted a fast alternation would rest on thresholds the text does not give, and one that found none could not show its list complete. For a video the methodology points to an outside analyser (PEAT), so the frames themselves have to be examined. So no check is linked and the entry is none. No axe rule is tagged for this test. The methodology's area threshold reads "inférieure à 21824" where the wording reads "inférieure ou égale"; the entry follows the wording. Applicability is judgment: whether anything on the page flashes is the same open question. Needs is media: an effect exists only over time, so examining it needs the engine's timed observation pass with media allowed to play.
